title: I numeri da zero a cento
summary: Counting 0-100, with the vowel-drop joins in the tens (ventuno, trentotto) and the accent on -tré

blocks.title: Zero, uno, due... i primi dieci
blocks.body: Numbers 1-10 you just have to **memorize** — there's no shortcut. Say them out loud a few times: *uno, due, tre, quattro, cinque, sei, sette, otto, nove, dieci*. Notice *sei* and *sette* look similar on the page but sound nothing alike out loud.
blocks.callout: Ten numbers, zero shortcuts — drill these until they're automatic.

blocks.title: Undici... venti: la famiglia -dici
blocks.body: 11-19 mostly follow the **-dici** pattern (like '-teen'): *tre-dici, quattor-dici, quin-dici*... but two numbers misbehave: **undici** (not *unodici*) and **sedici** (not *seidici* — the *s* comes first). **Venti** (20) is clean and regular — your launchpad for everything after.
blocks.callout: sedici flips the order — say it a few extra times so it sticks.

blocks.title: Da venti a cento: incolla i pezzi
blocks.body: From 20 on, Italian **glues pieces together** into one word. The tens: *venti, trenta, quaranta, cinquanta, sessanta, settanta, ottanta, novanta, cento*. To build a number in between, just add the units — **venti + due = ventidue**. Two traps: before **uno** and **otto** (both start with a vowel), the tens word **drops its final vowel** — *venti + uno = **ventuno*** (not *ventiuno*), *venti + otto = **ventotto***. And when a number ends in **tre**, it gets a written accent — *venti + tre = **ventitré***, *trenta + tre = **trentatré***.
blocks.callout: ventuno, ventotto, ventitré — memorize these three shapes and the rest of the century follows.

blocks.prompt: How do you write 21 in Italian?
blocks.explain: **ventuno** — venti drops its final *i* before a number starting with a vowel (uno).
**ventitré** — one word, and it takes a written accent because the stress falls on the final *é*.

blocks.hint: trenta + otto — remember the vowel drop.
blocks.explain: **trentotto** — trenta loses its final *a* before otto, the same trick as ventotto.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the number you hear.
Write out, in Italian words, your age, and one two-digit number you'd say out loud often (a house number, a bus number...). Use at least one vowel-drop number (like -uno or -otto).
